description: TEACHER-ONLY graded fork set for the 11.6 capstone. Each entry is a READING of something briefs/11.6-franchise.md deliberately leaves open, and every reading holds the other forks at the reference reading so a rejected test is attributable to one decision. ./gradlew generateForks builds a module per reading; ./gradlew verifyForks reports, per fork, whether the suite under test accepts exactly one (SETTLED) or several (LEFT OPEN). No reading is wrong — the report never names a right answer. Why this replaced the planned hidden corner-case set: every artifact we measured passed 7/7 of the settled corner cases, including a specification that disagreed with the reference on 884 of 3010 probed inputs, so a corner-case set graded nothing. Forks 1, 2 and 4 are the three that two independently written weak specifications both missed; fork 6 is here because nothing else asks whether the learner thought about an empty chain. Fork 3 (ties) is the VISIBLE practice tier and lives in the student build instead.

readings.label: both must admit — the chain's rule is a filter on top of each shop's
readings.note: The reference reading. 'The chain has rules of its own on top of that' reads most naturally as a filter.

readings.label: the shop decides alone — the chain's rule is not a gate on selling
readings.note: What every weak specification we measured actually implies: all three never mentioned Franchise.admissionPolicy at all. This is the single largest source of divergence in the corpus — 798 inputs where it sells and the reference says nobody will.

readings.label: the chain overrides — joining a chain replaces each shop's own door policy
readings.note: A real franchise model (central membership rules) and a plausible misreading of 'rules of its own on top of that'.

readings.label: both apply — the shop's first, the chain's on top
readings.note: The reference reading. Order is observable, so it is contract.

readings.label: both apply — the chain's first, the shop's on top
readings.note: Differs from the reference on 92 probed inputs: same shop, different price. Nothing in the brief picks a side.

readings.label: only the shop's promotions apply
readings.note: The brief lists 'the chain's, the shop's, both in sequence, or the better of the two' — so a one-sided reading is legitimate, not a defect. This is why two of the corner-case tests had to move out of the settled group: they each failed a reading the brief allows.

readings.label: only the chain's promotions apply
readings.note: The mirror of the above, and the one that makes 'the chain's own promotions reach the price' undecidable from the brief alone.

readings.label: price every shop fully, then take the cheapest
choose the cheapest shop on its own promotions, then apply the chain's to the winner
readings.note: The subtlest fork in the brief and the most fragile in practice: a conditional chain promotion makes these name DIFFERENT shops, and qwen2.5-coder:14b missed it even when implementing the frontier's specification. Only 2 of 3010 probed inputs separate them, so a suite that catches this is doing real work.

readings.label: no shops means nobody will sell, so there is no answer
readings.note: The reference reading, and what every agent we measured converged on without being asked.

readings.label: an empty chain is malformed, so asking it for an offer is an error
readings.note: Weakest pair in the set, kept deliberately: since every agent returns null here anyway, this fork measures whether the LEARNER thought about the empty chain, not whether an agent diverges. A suite that never builds one accepts both.
